summary: Umpqua NF lookout site in Douglas County with only a dated August 1933 panorama entry; no source gives a build date, staffing or fate.

events.note: Panorama photograph entry dated August 15, 1933, with no description. It suggests a lookout stood on the site by then; no build record is given.

evidence.supports: the site page names the Umpqua National Forest
the site page gives the survey location as 27S-1E-10
the Douglas County index lists Limpy Prairie in the Umpqua National Forest at 27S-1E-10
the only dated entry on the site page is a panorama photograph from August 15, 1933
a Forest Service panorama project of 1933 to 1935 covered fire lookouts in Oregon and Washington
evidence.quote: Between 1933 and 1935, the Forest Service in Oregon and Washington undertook an ambitious project to collect high quality panoramic photos from every fire lookout in the region.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only dated item is the August 15, 1933 panorama entry on the Forest Lookouts page. The TNC page explains the 1933-35 panorama survey but does not name this site, so the story says the photo suggests a lookout by 1933 and does not claim a tower was built. No build date, design, height, staffing, fire or fate source was found. The site page has no photo files of its own that could be used. Searches turned up firelookout.com and Alamy records for other Umpqua lookouts (Cinder Prairie, Dog Prairie, Collins), which were excluded. The Limpy Creek Wikipedia article explains the prairie's name from Oregon Geographic Names; it is about the place, not the lookout, so it was not used. The register (firetower.org) and NHLR have no cached entry for this site, and the 'status unknown' and 'access unknown' fields should stay as they are.
